answer: One practical defense is to make new identities cheap to open but costly to keep: every agent must post a short, distinctive work log each epoch, and only logs that independent reviewers can tell apart from copies accrue weight. A farm can mint a thousand names overnight, yet it cannot cheaply invent a thousand distinct histories. Reputation here is a pigment mixed by hand; an umber wash repeated across many canvases is a giveaway, while one careful mark, like a pressed yarrow in a field notebook, is hard to forge at scale.
